instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Name My Contribution
cards.instruction: Get them to acknowledge exactly what your effort, sacrifice, or strategy added to the result.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When you thank the festival team, say I repaired the stage in the rain. Remember our speech practice: tell them what somebody did, not just that they were wonderful.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll thank everyone equally.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A generous opening; you used to forget half the team. Now give me one equal sentence about replacing those rotten boards.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You want your name in the speech?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: With the work beside it: tell them I replaced the boards so the dancers could perform. Read that sentence back to me, with the verb left in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell the trip committee what my spreadsheet did. You used to write 'very helpful' on every report until I made you explain the help.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It helped enormously.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A bigger adjective. Now use a verb: what did it let you do with the bookings?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Recover the ones missing from our list.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All thirty. Say I rebuilt the list so thirty people kept their seats. Put that in your report before you thank me; that's the explanation we practised.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Pick the Prize
cards.instruction: Make them choose which reward, principle, or relationship matters most when not everything can be kept.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Choose the trophy ceremony or our anniversary dinner. Both start at seven, and the restaurant won't hold our table. I taught you to check a diary before promising me an evening.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we celebrate afterward?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A plan with a time in it, at least. But afterward loses the table. Are you keeping your promise to me or collecting the trophy?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The ceremony might be short.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Short doesn't help; they start together. Put one appointment in your diary and cross the other out, like we practised. Which one stays?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The team bus costs exactly your prize money. Keep the money or pay for the trip—which matters more? We did this budgeting together when you first joined.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't we book a cheaper bus?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you checked the biggest cost first. That is the cheapest quote, the one I made you get in writing. There isn't another saving to find.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're making me look selfish.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then make the choice plainly, as I taught you. Are you keeping the prize, or are we telling the team their bus is paid for? I won't quietly divide the bill among them.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Lose Something for Me
cards.instruction: Create a loyalty test by asking them to accept a real disadvantage on your behalf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me serve first in the final, even if it costs you the match. Your old coach could use that advantage; I taught you to support the person beside you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You taught me to compete. Why give you the first serve?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A good memory when it suits you. You said you were on my side today; let me see it when there's a point to lose.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant I'd be pleased for you if you won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose to receive and give your old coach the first serve. You can still try to beat me afterward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Miss the prize ceremony and come to my opening night. I sat through your first performances and taught you to keep going when the room was empty.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm receiving the prize.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Look at you, worth a whole ceremony now. Send someone to collect it. I'd like one familiar face who gave up something to be there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's an unfair test of whether I care.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the prize; give me the evening they hand it over. I taught you to play to one person when nobody else stayed. Be that person for me tonight.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Concede the Point
cards.instruction: Get them to release one claim, advantage, or disputed victory without reopening the entire contest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Concede that one ball was out. Keep the match. I taught you to watch where it lands, not who hit it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does it matter if I still win?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're separating two things at last. The ball landed beyond the line; I'd like you to call that accurately even with the trophy in your hand.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're not asking for a rematch?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. Say 'out', the way we practised calling a line. Then take your trophy home; I won't make you play for it again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Admit I found the restaurant. Keep credit for the holiday. Remember how I taught you to look down the side streets instead of following every sign?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You complained about the menu.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A sharp memory for the wrong detail. We can dislike the soup and still agree who found the door. Just give me that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. You found it. The rest was my itinerary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. You've learnt to plan a whole week without me. I'll take credit for the restaurant and leave you the rest.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: I Changed the Odds
cards.instruction: Hide how your own choice tilted the contest, bargain, or consequence while continuing to judge the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My cake deserved first prize. You can congratulate your old teacher; I spent years showing you how to present a sponge properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why did you move yours under the judging light?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just tidying the display. You're noticing presentation at last. The judges still had to taste it, and mine earned the ribbon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You left mine in the shade.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put better lighting on next year's checklist. I taught you to learn from a result, not reopen it; tell me what you thought of my winning sponge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That raffle was a fair draw. Read the result out; I taught you to announce a winner clearly, not mumble into the prize table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You folded your own ticket differently.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For filing. Good eye, though you used to need me to read every ticket for you. The number still won fairly; read it out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can feel which ticket is yours without looking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hands out of the bowl now. The draw's finished. Use the voice we practised and congratulate me.
